node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Paired numerical data
node.description: Recognise paired numerical data as two measurements recorded for each case or individual.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Explanatory and response variables
node.description: Distinguish explanatory and response variables in a bivariate statistical context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Plot paired data
node.description: Plot paired numerical data as points on coordinate axes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scatterplot axes and scales
node.description: Choose and interpret axes, labels and scales for scatterplots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Read scatterplots
node.description: Read individual points and overall visual patterns in scatterplots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scatterplot clusters and outliers
node.description: Identify clusters, gaps and unusual points in scatterplots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Direction of association
node.description: Describe positive, negative or no association in paired numerical data.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Form of association
node.description: Describe whether an association appears linear, curved or has another form.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Strength of association
node.description: Describe how tightly paired data follow an overall pattern.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Correlation coefficient introduction
node.description: Interpret correlation coefficient as a numerical summary of direction and strength for linear association.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Correlation versus causation
node.description: Distinguish statistical association from evidence of cause-and-effect.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Line of best fit visual estimate
node.description: Use a visual line of best fit to summarise a roughly linear bivariate pattern.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Interpret slope and intercept in context
node.description: Interpret slope and intercept of a fitted linear model in the context of paired data.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Residuals introduction
node.description: Interpret residuals as vertical differences between observed values and model predictions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Sample to population claims
node.description: Use sample data cautiously to make claims about a population.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Sampling variability
node.description: Recognise that different samples from the same population can produce different results.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Informal confidence language
node.description: Use cautious language to express uncertainty in informal statistical claims.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Margin of error introduction
node.description: Interpret margin of error informally as a range of plausible error around a sample estimate.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare sample groups
node.description: Compare sample groups while considering sample size, variability and overlap.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Inference from random samples
node.description: Use random samples as evidence for population claims while recognising uncertainty.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Limits of informal inference
node.description: Recognise limits of claims based on sample design, variability, bias and context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Paired data preserve cases
node.description: Each point in a bivariate data set represents two values from the same case or individual.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scatterplots show paired values
node.description: Scatterplots display paired numerical values as coordinate points.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Association has direction form and strength
node.description: Association is described using direction, form, strength and unusual points.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Correlation summarises linear association
node.description: Correlation describes direction and strength of a linear association, not all patterns.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Correlation is not causation
node.description: A correlation alone does not establish that one variable causes the other.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Line of best fit models trend
node.description: A line of best fit summarises an overall linear trend and does not usually pass through every point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Residual is observed minus predicted
node.description: A residual compares an observed response value with the value predicted by a model.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Samples vary naturally
node.description: Different samples can give different estimates even when drawn from the same population.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Inference claims need uncertainty
node.description: Claims from samples should acknowledge uncertainty, sample design and variability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Random samples support population claims
node.description: Random samples can support population claims better than convenience samples, though uncertainty remains.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unpaired values treated as points
node.description: Learner plots two unrelated lists as if values in matching positions form meaningful pairs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Correlation means causation
node.description: Learner assumes an association proves that one variable causes the other.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Strong correlation from two points
node.description: Learner judges strong association from too few points or isolated aligned points.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Line of best fit must hit all points
node.description: Learner thinks a line of best fit must pass through every data point or the most points possible.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Sample claim without uncertainty
node.description: Learner states a population claim from sample data as certain and exact.

edge.rationale: Paired numerical data are the data structure represented in scatterplots.
Explanatory and response variables support interpretation of bivariate scatterplots.
Plotting paired data directly practises scatterplot construction.
Axes and scales are essential scatterplot conventions.
Reading scatterplots is central to bivariate display interpretation.
Clusters and outliers are important scatterplot features.
Direction is a core descriptor of association.
Form is a core descriptor of association patterns.
Strength describes how tightly points follow an association pattern.
Correlation coefficient formalises linear association strength and direction.
Correlation-versus-causation reasoning is central to interpreting association responsibly.
Lines of best fit summarise roughly linear association visually.
Slope and intercept interpretation connects fitted lines to bivariate context.
Residuals extend model interpretation by comparing observations with predictions.
Sample-to-population claims are central to informal inference.
Sampling variability is central to informal inference.
Informal confidence language helps express uncertainty in claims.
Margin of error is an accessible bridge toward formal inference.
Comparing sample groups applies informal inference to group differences.
Random samples support stronger population inference than convenience samples.
Understanding limits of inference helps avoid overclaiming from sample data.
Paired numerical data requires recognising numerical variables and how data are recorded.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats paired values as separate unconnected lists.

edge.rationale: Explanatory and response variables are identified within paired bivariate data contexts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot say which variable is used to help explain or predict the other.

edge.rationale: Plotting paired data requires locating ordered pairs on coordinate axes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot turn paired values into plotted coordinate points.

edge.rationale: Axes and scales are chosen to plot paired data clearly.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots points but uses unreadable or inconsistent axes.

edge.rationale: Reading scatterplots requires interpreting axes, scales and plotted points.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads points without attending to axes or scale values.

edge.rationale: Recognising clusters and outliers builds from reading scatterplots accurately.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sees individual points but not unusual points or clustered regions.

edge.rationale: Direction of association is inferred from the overall scatterplot pattern.
edge.failure_signal: Learner describes a single point rather than the overall direction of the data cloud.

edge.rationale: Form of association builds on recognising an overall association pattern.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calls every pattern linear without considering curvature or other form.

edge.rationale: Strength is judged relative to how closely points follow the observed form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner judges strength from slope steepness rather than scatter around the pattern.

edge.rationale: Correlation coefficient formalises visual strength and direction for linear association.
edge.failure_signal: Learner interprets correlation without understanding visual association strength.

edge.rationale: Correlation-versus-causation reasoning builds from interpreting association and correlation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats any correlation as causal evidence.

edge.rationale: A line of best fit is useful when a scatterplot has an approximately linear form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws a fitted line for non-linear or patternless data without justification.

edge.rationale: Interpreting slope and intercept in fitted lines requires linear-function meaning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner states slope and intercept numerically without contextual meaning.

edge.rationale: Residuals compare observed values with values predicted by a fitted line.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify prediction error for a point relative to a model.

edge.rationale: Sample-to-population claims require understanding samples, populations and representativeness.
edge.failure_signal: Learner makes a population claim from any data set without considering sample design.

edge.rationale: Sampling variability builds on recognising natural variability in repeated data or samples.
edge.failure_signal: Learner expects all samples from a population to give identical summaries.

edge.rationale: Informal confidence language expresses uncertainty in sample-to-population claims.
edge.failure_signal: Learner states sample-based claims as exact facts.

edge.rationale: Margin of error is an informal summary of uncertainty from sampling variability.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a sample estimate as exact without a plausible range.

edge.rationale: Comparing sample groups uses distribution comparison plus uncertainty from sampling.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares groups using a single statistic without considering overlap or variability.

edge.rationale: Inference from random samples depends on understanding why random selection supports population claims.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats convenience samples as equally strong evidence as random samples.

edge.rationale: Limits of inference depend on identifying bias, sample design problems and uncertainty.
edge.failure_signal: Learner overgeneralises from biased or limited data.
